title.narrative: Strengthening the roles of science granting councils in Africa's science systems

description.narrative:
The Programme titled “Strengthening the roles of science granting councils in Africa’s science systems“ is a partnership between IDRC, Norad and South Africa’s National Research Foundation (NRF). This Programme is part of the Science Granting Councils Initiative phase 2 (SGCI-2), which seeks to strengthen capacities of 16 science granting councils in sub-Saharan Africa. The SGCI participating countries are Botswana, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Namibia, Nigeria, Mozambique, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
The expected Impact is strong national science systems that contribute to economic and social development in sub-Saharan Africa. The expected Outcome is more effective investments by the Councils in research, development and innovation. To meet these goals, the Programme has four interrelated objectives:
i) Support research projects with potential for commercialization and upscaling and carried out in partnership with the private sector/ industry and social sector including community-based organizations and groups. Support fundamental research projects that can contribute to global stock of knowledge and build new research fields; ii) Strengthen the Councils’ research management systems and practices; iii) Promote gender equality and inclusivity; and iv) Support knowledge sharing, interactive learning and networking among researchers, Councils and other actors
The direct target group is science granting councils and the intended end target groups are research actors, private sector actors and social sector actors.
